items.title: Keith Ingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: But Kenton was one of their inspirations.

ctx.x: Mostly from records, because we didn’t get American musicians coming to England at the time when I was growing up, because there was a musician’s union ban I think on

both sides. Certainly the English musician’s union didn’t want American artists coming in, like jazz musicians, because they said it would take work away from the local musicians. Well in a sense that’s probably true, but also, we couldn’t get to hear these wonderful people who were still playing. And I bitterly regretted it because they were over in Paris. Quite a lot of them came to Paris. I was too young to get over there on my own. And I never forgot the first time Stan Kenton’s orchestra, which was very…
I remember, you know Derek Smith?
